court: In the High Court of Madras†
judges_raw: (Before S.M. Subramaniam and K. Surender, JJ.)
respondents: District Collector, Namakkal District and Others
case_number: WP No. 546 of 2022 and WMP No. 584 of 2022
advocates: For Respondents: Mr. T. Arunkumar, Addl. Govt. Pleader
judgment_text:
Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying to issue a writ of certiorari, to call for the records on the file of the 3rd respondent in relation to the impugned eviction Notice dated 24-12-2021 issued vide Na.ka. No. 684/2010/A1 pertaining to the petitioner's land situated in Punjai Idaiyar Melmugam Village, Paramathi - Velur Taluk, Namakkal District comprised in S. Nos. 576/27 & 576/28 and quash the same as the petitioner's land is a ‘Natham Vacant Land’

The Order of the Court was delivered by

S.M. Subramaniam, J.:— The notice for eviction issued by the Executive Authority, Velur Selection Grade Town Panchayat is under challenge in the present Writ Petition.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the subject land is Village Natham land and therefore the eviction proceedings ought not to have been initiated by the Authority.

3. The learned Additional Government Pleader would oppose by stating that even as per the judgments of this Court, if Village Natham land is an unoccupied land, then the Government is empowered to evict the encroachments, if any. As per the proceedings of the Executive Authority, the subject land has been identified as unoccupied. Therefore, there is no impediment for initiating eviction proceedings.

4. May that as it be, even in respect of the Government Natham land, the assignment is to be granted for occupation. In the absence of any valid assignment in accordance with the Revenue Standing Orders, it is not as if any person can go and occupy the land and claim right over such land.

5. In the present case, the proceedings of the Executive Authority would show that it is an unoccupied Village Natham. Thus, the Government is empowered to regulate the land in accordance with the Revenue Standing Orders and Laws in force. That being the factum, there is no impediment for the Authorities to proceed with the enforcement action by following the procedures as contemplated under law.

6. Accordingly, the present Writ Petition stands dismissed. No costs. Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
